The near fae rides a papery blade-seed down with both arms wrapped round its blade, wings shut flat, leaning hard left to steer it toward the sack and losing the argument entirely.
She grabs a second grown fae's ankle as the gust takes her, both of them now horizontal, streaming out like a flag over the drop, her free hand still clutching a full net.
He sits square on a bucking sack with both boots braced wide and both fists white-knuckled on the rim, the down pushing out between his fingers in a slow triumphant column.
The near fae runs flat out underneath a spinning tuft with the net held up in both hands, head tilted all the way back, watching it and running clean off the stem's edge.
She hauls a loaded sack along the stem with a cord biting over one shoulder, leaning so far forward her chin nearly touches the stalk, the sack dragging and twisting behind her.
A second grown fae close beside her stamps a lid down onto a pail with one boot while the down bulges out at every seam and one small hooked ball sails serenely over them both.
The near fae hangs off a sailing tuft by both hands with her boots kicked straight up, one boot already gone, tumbling away below on its own independent journey toward the drop.
He flicks a swollen pod with one fingertip and takes the whole spray of it square in the face, eyes sealed, hand still raised, a second pod already swelling on the stem beside him.
She is wrapped to the shoulders in a whole drift of down, only her face and one outstretched arm visible, fingers spread, reaching for a papery blade-seed that has already made its decision.
The near fae catches a climbing stem hand over hand with a full net swinging from her teeth, the net swinging wide on each heave and shedding two tufts back into the wind.
A second grown fae close beside her picks hooked balls off the near fae's wing one at a time, lobbing each one high over the drop, a woven sack pinned under her own knee meanwhile.
She is thrown flat on her back by a sudden squall, wings pinned under her, the air above her gone solid white with everything the gust took off the stand in one breath.
He spits a mouthful of down mid-sentence, still hauling on the cord of a sack that has swollen to twice his size and is dragging him back along the stem toward the rim.

The near fae reaches right out over the drop after a papery blade-seed already three arm-lengths gone, one boot on the stem's edge, her whole body cantilevered right out over the drop, and still short.
She is caught mid-leap with one hand out and both boots already off the stem, a full net trailing behind her, the tuft she is after already a handspan higher and accelerating upward.
He ducks hard as a papery blade-seed whips past at exactly head height, hair blown flat across his face, and straightens just in time to take the next one across the ear.
The near fae shakes a rattling head upside down over a cupped shell with both hands and her whole shoulders in it, down streaming out sideways in the shove of the wind.
A second grown fae close beside her holds the mouth of a sack shut with both fists while it fills and swells, her wings hammering to keep her upright as the sack goes round.
She braces one boot on a second grown fae's back and hauls a hooked ball out of his wing with both hands, both of them leaning hard opposite ways, neither one winning yet.
The near fae scrambles after a pod that has sprung off the stalk and is cartwheeling along the stem rim, slapping it down with both palms flat, her chin level with the stem's surface.
He wraps both arms round an armful of down that is escaping upward faster than he can follow, his wings beating full open, his chin buried in it, rising off the stem against his will.
She sits on the sack to hold the lid down, plainly losing, one whole side of down already escaping in a rope straight up, a river pebble still sitting squarely on the lid, overruled.
The near fae is knocked sideways by a gust that lays the whole stand over at once, hanging off the bent stem with both legs out horizontal, a net still looped over one wrist.
A second grown fae close beside her hauls a spinning papery blade-seed out of the air by its blade with both hands, twisting hard to bring it down, her boots skidding on the stem.
He reaches between a second grown fae's wings with two fingers and plucks a hooked ball clean out of her feathers, the ball immediately catching his own sleeve and sticking there instead.
